name: AdaptlyPost
description: Draft, schedule, publish and measure social media posts on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile, Tumblr, Telegram and WordPress, with bulk and recurring posts, RSS feeds, webhooks, AI captions and images, and post analytics. Sign in with OAuth or an API key.
author: AdaptlyPost

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces this sign-in can act in, across every organization the user belongs to. Returns { workspaces } with id, name, organization { id, name }, role { key, name }, permissions (the permission keys held there), isDefault, current and can { draft, schedule, publish }. Call this when the user names a workspace, brand, client or organization, or when accounts or posts they expect are missing: then pass the matching id as workspaceId to every other tool. Without workspaceId, tools act in the workspace marked current. An API key belongs to one workspace, so it lists only that one. Takes no arguments.

result.description: An object with workspaces: one { id, name, organization, role, permissions, isDefault, current, can } per workspace. Pass id as workspaceId to other tools.

tools.name: get_me
tools.title: Get My Access
tools.description: Describe this connection in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another): whether it is an API key or a sign-in, its role, the permission keys it holds, can { draft, schedule, publish } and a one-sentence summary of what it may do. An API key never holds more than the member who created it (issuerRole). Call this before an action the role may not allow, instead of trying and reading a 403. Takes only the optional workspaceId.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with tokenType (api_token or oauth), tokenId, tokenName, workspace { id }, organizationId, role { key, name }, issuerRole, permissions, can { draft, schedule, publish }, summary and expiresAt (null for a key that never expires).

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.title: List Connected Accounts
tools.description: List the social accounts connected to the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) across all fourteen platforms. Returns { accounts } with id, platform, displayName, username, avatarUrl, status, pageId for Facebook pages, and supportsInstagramAudio for Instagram (true when the account can add audio to Reels, see search_instagram_audio). For a Pinterest account, list_pinterest_boards returns the boards it can pin to; for a WordPress site, list_wordpress_categories returns its categories. For a Google Business Profile location displayName is the location title and username is empty; its id goes in googleBusinessConnectionIds. status is active or unauthorized; an unauthorized account (unauthorizedReason carries the platform's message) is refused with 400 by create_post until the user reconnects it in AdaptlyPost, so leave it out and tell the user. Call this before create_post, update_post, or bulk_schedule_posts: they take these ids, never usernames. Pass the ids as accountIds, or put each id in the array for its platform (linkedinConnectionIds, tumblrConnectionIds, telegramConnectionIds, wordpressConnectionIds, and so on); Facebook page accounts go in pageIds. check_account re-checks a Facebook page with Facebook, and remove_account disconnects an account. Not for post history or publishing status: use list_posts or list_post_results for those. Takes only the optional workspaceId.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with accounts: one { id, platform, displayName, username, avatarUrl, status } per connected account, plus unauthorizedReason when status is unauthorized, pageId for Facebook pages and supportsInstagramAudio for Instagram. Use id as the connection id (or in pageIds for Facebook).

tools.name: search_instagram_audio
tools.title: Search Instagram Audio
tools.description: Search Instagram music and original sounds to add to a Reel. Returns { audio } with audioId, audioType, title, displayArtist (music), igUsername (original sounds), durationMs, coverArtworkUrl, profilePictureUrl, previewUrl (a temporary audio file, expires after about 1.5 days), instagramUrl and isAdsEligible. Leave out searchQuery to get what is trending. Only audio Meta has cleared for third-party publishing comes back, which can differ from what the Instagram app shows. Only works for Instagram accounts with supportsInstagramAudio: true in list_accounts; otherwise, or when Instagram rejects the search, it fails with 400. Pass the chosen audioId, with its title and artist, in instagramConfigs[].audio of create_post, update_post or bulk_schedule_posts. Nothing is posted.

accountId.description: The Instagram account id from list_accounts

audioType.description: music for licensed tracks, original_sound for sounds from other Instagram posts

searchQuery.description: Keyword filter (max 100 characters). Leave out for trending audio

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with audio: one { audioId, audioType, title, displayArtist, igUsername, durationMs, coverArtworkUrl, profilePictureUrl, previewUrl, instagramUrl, isAdsEligible } per match. Pass audioId as instagramConfigs[].audio.audioId.

tools.name: list_pinterest_boards
tools.title: List Pinterest Boards
tools.description: List the boards of a connected Pinterest account, secret boards included. Returns { boards } with id, name, description, privacy (PUBLIC, PROTECTED or SECRET) and pinCount. Call it before posting to Pinterest, ask the user which board to pin to unless they already named one, and pass that board's id as pinterestConfigs[].boardId in create_post, update_post or bulk_schedule_posts. When the user named a board you may pass that name as boardName instead, never both; a name that matches no board, or several, fails with 400 and nothing falls back. A board belongs to one Pinterest account, so call it once per Pinterest account. A post sent without boardId or boardName goes to a public board named AdaptlyPost, which is created on first use. Fails with 404 when accountId is not a Pinterest account in the workspace, and with 400 when Pinterest refuses the request, which usually means the user must reconnect the account in AdaptlyPost. Nothing is posted.

accountId.description: The Pinterest account id from list_accounts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with boards: one { id, name, description, privacy, pinCount } per board. Pass id as pinterestConfigs[].boardId, or name as boardName.

tools.name: list_wordpress_categories
tools.title: List WordPress Categories
tools.description: List the categories of a connected WordPress site, sorted by name. Returns { categories } with id, name and parentId (null for a top-level category). Call it when the user names categories for a WordPress post, match the names to ids, and pass those ids as wordpressConfigs[].categoryIds in create_post, update_post or bulk_schedule_posts. Categories belong to one site, so call it once per WordPress account. A post sent without categoryIds goes to the site's default category. Fails with 404 when accountId is not a WordPress account in the workspace, and with an error carrying the reason when the site refuses the request or cannot be reached, which may mean the user must reconnect the site in AdaptlyPost. Nothing is posted.

accountId.description: The WordPress account id from list_accounts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with categories: one { id, name, parentId } per category. Pass id in wordpressConfigs[].categoryIds.

tools.name: check_account
tools.title: Check Account
tools.description: Re-check a Facebook page with Facebook now, using its stored token, and return its fresh status. A rejected token marks the page unauthorized (unauthorizedReason carries Facebook's message); a working token clears an earlier unauthorized mark. Facebook pages only: any other account fails with 400. Pages are also checked automatically twice a day. Use it after the user reconnects or fixes a page, or when a Facebook post failed with a token error. Needs the accounts.manage permission, which Admin holds. Nothing is posted.

accountId.description: The Facebook account id from list_accounts, or its pageId

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with id, platform, displayName, pageId, status (active or unauthorized), unauthorizedReason when unauthorized, and checkedAt.

tools.name: remove_account
tools.title: Remove Account
tools.description: Disconnect a social account from the workspace, the same way the Connectors page does: its stored tokens are deleted, it is taken off every pending and recurring post, and it stops counting toward the plan. Works for accounts in any status, so an unauthorized account can be cleaned up without reconnecting it. For Facebook only the named page goes; the other pages of the same login stay connected. Posts already published stay on the network. Confirm with the user first, naming the account. Bringing it back means connecting it again in AdaptlyPost (create_connect_link can send a link). Needs the accounts.manage permission, which Admin holds.

accountId.description: The account id from list_accounts, or the Facebook pageId

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with id, platform, displayName, pageId for Facebook, and removed: true.

tools.name: create_connect_link
tools.title: Create Connect Link
tools.description: Create a link someone else, such as a client, opens to connect their social accounts to this workspace without an AdaptlyPost login. With no options it is a quick link: it lasts 7 days, offers every platform, shows the client every account in the workspace and connects any number of accounts. visibility PRIVATE shows the client only the accounts they connected through the link; allowedPlatforms limits the platforms offered; maxAccounts makes the link stop working once that many accounts are connected through it; expiresAt or neverExpires changes when it stops working. Returns the url to send. Connected accounts then show up in list_accounts. Revoke it with revoke_connect_link. Needs the accounts.manage permission, which Admin holds.

name.description: Label shown in the dashboard list of links (max 80 characters)

visibility.description: PRIVATE shows the client only the accounts they connected through this link. Defaults to PUBLIC

allowedPlatforms.description: Platforms the client can pick. Omit or send [] for every platform

maxAccounts.description: Accounts the link can connect in total. Reconnecting an account it already connected does not count again

expiresAt.description: When the link stops working, as an ISO 8601 date-time with a Z or ±hh:mm offset (e.g. "2026-11-30T23:59:59Z"). At least 1 hour and at most 365 days from now. Defaults to 7 days from now. Leave it out when neverExpires is true

neverExpires.description: true keeps the link working until it is revoked or reaches maxAccounts. Cannot be combined with expiresAt

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with url (the link to send), token (pass it to revoke_connect_link), expiresAt (null when it never expires), name, visibility, allowedPlatforms and maxAccounts.

tools.name: revoke_connect_link
tools.title: Revoke Connect Link
tools.description: Revoke a connect link so it stops working at once. Accounts already connected through it stay connected; remove them with remove_account. Needs the accounts.manage permission, which Admin holds. Returns { success: true }.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with success: true once the link is revoked.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.title: Upload Media
tools.description: Upload images, videos or documents to AdaptlyPost storage and return public URLs for the mediaUrls of create_post, update_post, or bulk_schedule_posts. Three sources, combinable in one call: attachments (files the user attached in a ChatGPT conversation, which ChatGPT passes as file references; use this for every file attached in ChatGPT, whatever its size), urls (public https URLs the server streams straight into storage; private, internal and non-https addresses are refused) and files (base64 data, for small media attached in other apps; 30 MB decoded per call in total). Omitting all three returns an error. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4 and QuickTime, plus PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC and DOCX for LinkedIn DOCUMENT posts, checked by file content (and, for Office files, the extension, so keep it in the name or URL); 50 MB per image, 100 MB per document, 250 MB per attachment or URL download. Stored files are public immediately, post or no post, so only upload media the user supplied or asked for. For base64 files over 30 MB use get_upload_urls and PUT the bytes yourself. Returns uploaded ({ publicUrl, key } per file) and mediaUrls; pass mediaUrls straight into the post. One publicUrl may be reused across any number of posts; the file is kept until the last post referencing it has published, so upload once and reuse rather than re-uploading per post.

download_url.description: Temporary download URL of the attached file

file_id.description: ChatGPT file id of the attached file

mime_type.description: MIME type of the attached file

file_name.description: Name of the attached file, with its extension

attachments.description: Files the user attached in the ChatGPT conversation: images, videos or documents, up to 250 MB each. ChatGPT fills in each file reference; put every attached file the user wants to post here

urls.description: Public https URLs of images, videos or documents to upload (e.g. ["https://example.com/photo.jpg", "https://example.com/deck.pdf"])

files.description: Direct file uploads as base64, 30 MB decoded per call in total. Use this for small media attached in apps other than ChatGPT; in ChatGPT use attachments

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with uploaded (array of { publicUrl, key } per file) and mediaUrls (the public URLs ready to pass to create_post).

tools.name: get_upload_urls
tools.title: Get Media Upload URLs
tools.description: Get presigned upload URLs for direct file uploads. Returns uploadUrl (PUT your file here) and publicUrl (use in create_post mediaUrls). This only mints a URL. You MUST PUT the file to uploadUrl and confirm a 2xx response before using publicUrl, otherwise create_post/bulk rejects it with "Media file(s) not found in storage". If the PUT cannot reach uploadUrl, for example a sandbox network proxy answers 403 or the storage host is not on its allowlist, do not retry it, do not stop, and never put the files in a public repo or file-sharing link: call open_upload_widget and have the user add the files through the upload box or upload link it returns. If the files are ones you made, hand them to the user as downloads first. Prefer upload_media for public URLs and for inline files under 30 MB; use this for larger files you hold yourself. For each file, provide fileName and mimeType. Supported types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif (Facebook, X, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn, Tumblr and WordPress only), video/mp4, video/quicktime, and for LinkedIn DOCUMENT posts application/pdf, application/vnd.ms-powerpoint, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation, application/msword and application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document; keep the extension in fileName, since the post reads the file type from it. A publicUrl may be reused across any number of posts; the file is kept until the last post referencing it has published.

files.description: Files to get upload URLs for

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with urls: one { uploadUrl, publicUrl, key } entry per requested file.

tools.name: open_upload_widget
tools.title: Upload From Device
tools.description: Let the user add photos, videos or documents from their phone or computer. Use it when the user wants to post a file that has no public URL, such as a photo on their phone, a file attached in the chat that upload_media cannot read (in ChatGPT, pass attached files to upload_media as attachments instead), or a file you built in a sandbox whose network blocks the get_upload_urls uploadUrl. Never suggest putting the files in a public GitHub repo or a file-sharing link instead. In apps that show MCP Apps widgets, such as ChatGPT and Claude chat, it shows an upload box in the chat, and when the upload finishes the box sends a message listing the public media URLs. In apps that cannot show the box, such as Claude Cowork and Claude Code, it returns status upload_link with uploadUrl, a page the user opens in their browser to upload, and uploadId: give the user the link, wait until they say they finished, then call this tool again with that uploadId to get the media URLs. Pass the media URLs as mediaUrls to create_post, update_post or bulk_schedule_posts. Nothing is uploaded until the user picks files. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, QuickTime, PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC and DOCX, up to 250 MB per file, 50 MB per image and 100 MB per document. Uploaded files are stored at public URLs.

uploadId.description: uploadId from an earlier call that returned an upload link. Returns the files the user uploaded through that link instead of opening a new upload.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: Without uploadId: status waiting_for_upload when the upload box is shown (the media URLs arrive later in a message from the box), or status upload_link with uploadUrl, uploadId and acceptsUntil. With uploadId: status (waiting, saving, ready, failed or expired), files ({ fileName, publicUrl } each), mediaUrls, failed ({ fileName, error } each), savingCount and acceptsUntil.

tools.name: get_upload_ticket
tools.title: Get Upload Ticket
tools.description: Called by the upload box that open_upload_widget shows, once per file, to authorize storing that file in AdaptlyPost media storage. Returns a ticket valid for 5 minutes. Do not call this yourself; call open_upload_widget instead.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with expiresAt and uploadUrl for the upload box.

tools.name: create_post
tools.title: Create Post
tools.description: Create one post on the user's own connected social accounts. saveAsDraft saves a DRAFT and publishes nothing; a scheduledAt sent with it becomes the draft's planned date, which publish_draft later schedules. Without saveAsDraft, a future scheduledAt schedules the post; otherwise it publishes now. Before publishing or scheduling, show the user the final text, media, accounts and time (or repeat schedule) and get their confirmation; a draft needs no confirmation. Account ids come from list_accounts (pass them as accountIds, or as platforms plus the per-platform arrays) and mediaUrls from upload_media. Platform-specific options (TikTok privacy, Pinterest board, LinkedIn document or reshare, Google Business event or offer, Tumblr tags, WordPress title, excerpt, categories and tags, YouTube audio language, Instagram user tags, Facebook link carousel, first comments, threads of replies, recurrence) are described on each field. To find every problem before creating anything, call validate_post with the same input first. Publishing runs per platform in the background, so the response ({ postId, queuedPlatforms, isScheduled, scheduledAt }) is not the outcome; check list_post_results. Each call creates a separate post, so after an error or timeout check list_posts before trying again. Use update_post or publish_draft for an existing post and bulk_schedule_posts for many posts.

text.description: Default post text shared across platforms. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

accountIds.description: Account ids (or Facebook pageIds) from list_accounts to post to. AdaptlyPost adds each account's platform to platforms and its id to the matching connection-id array, so you can send these instead of platforms and the per-platform arrays, or alongside them. An id not connected to the workspace fails with 400

platforms.description: Target platforms (e.g. ["LINKEDIN", "TWITTER"]). Each one needs its matching connection-id array (pageIds for FACEBOOK, googleBusinessConnectionIds for GOOGLE_BUSINESS) filled with ids from list_accounts. Optional when accountIds is sent

contentType.description: Content type: TEXT, IMAGE, VIDEO, CAROUSEL, or DOCUMENT. Must match mediaUrls. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on TWITTER, BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. DOCUMENT publishes one PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (max 100 MB, 300 pages) as a LinkedIn document post and is LinkedIn only: put exactly that one file in mediaUrls, target only LINKEDIN, and set the title with linkedinConfigs

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant to schedule (e.g. "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"). Omit to post immediately; a past time also posts immediately. With saveAsDraft it is the draft's planned date instead: nothing is scheduled, and publish_draft without a date later schedules the draft for it

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with the post for display (e.g. "America/New_York"); it does not shift scheduledAt

saveAsDraft.description: Save as DRAFT instead of publishing or scheduling; publish later with publish_draft. A scheduledAt sent with it is stored as the draft's planned date, and publish_draft schedules the draft for that date

frequency.description: How often the post repeats: DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or YEARLY. YEARLY repeats on the same date; a series started on February 29 posts on February 28 in other years

interval.description: Repeat every N days, weeks, months or years, 1 to 30 (default 1)

weekdays.description: WEEKLY only: the weekdays it goes out on (e.g. ["MONDAY", "THURSDAY"]). The weekday of scheduledAt is always included

endsOn.description: Last day an occurrence may go out on, as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Must be on or after the day of the first post. Cannot be combined with maxOccurrences

maxOccurrences.description: Total number of posts the series publishes, 2 to 365. Cannot be combined with endsOn; omit both to repeat until the user pauses or deletes the series

recurrence.description: Repeat the post on a schedule the user asked for, and confirm that schedule with them first. Needs a future scheduledAt, which becomes the first post and sets the time of day in timezone. Cannot be combined with saveAsDraft or TIKTOK. Missed slots, for example while paused, are skipped and never published late. The user can pause or stop the series at any time with pause_recurring_post or delete_recurring_post; list_recurring_posts shows it

mediaUrls.description: Media URLs to attach. Use publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls; the same publicUrl may be reused across posts. Do not reuse mediaUrls read back from a published post, which may be expiring platform links

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (max 1000 characters each; use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile and videos ignore it

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it
The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account right after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment is posted about 10 seconds after the platform publishes (60 on YouTube) and retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long reply, more than 25 replies, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

twitterKeepLinks.description: Keep links in the X text clickable. X charges over 10 times more for a post with a link, so by default every link in X text is broken (example.com becomes example. com). Only AppSumo lifetime deals can turn this on, and a kept link costs 20 credits instead of 2. true on any other plan is refused with 400; it is ignored when the X text has no link

linkedinConnectionIds.description: LinkedIn account connection IDs to post from

twitterConnectionIds.description: X (Twitter) account connection IDs to post from

tumblrConnectionIds.description: Tumblr blogs to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TUMBLR takes text up to 32768 characters, up to 30 JPEG, PNG or GIF images (10 MB each) or one MP4 video (500 MB, up to 10 minutes), and alt text; it has no first comments, threads, per-platform thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

telegramConnectionIds.description: Telegram channels and groups to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media

wordpressConnectionIds.description: WordPress sites to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. A site without an entry in wordpressConfigs uses the first line of the text as the title. WordPress has no first comments, threads, thumbnails, image shapes or analytics

googleBusinessConnectionIds.description: Google Business Profile locations to post to, by the account id from list_accounts. A location without an entry in googleBusinessConfigs gets a STANDARD update

pageIds.description: Facebook page account ids from list_accounts (the account id; its pageId value is also accepted). Facebook has no connection-id array

title.description: Video title (max 90 chars)

caption.description: TikTok-specific caption: up to 2200 characters on a video, 4000 on a photo or photo carousel post

allowComments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok post

allowDuet.description: Allow other users to Duet this video

allowStitch.description: Allow other users to Stitch this video

allowEmbedding.description: Allow embedding the video on other sites

madeForKids.description: Mark the video as made for kids (COPPA)

defaultAudioLanguage.description: Language spoken in the video's original audio, as a BCP-47 tag such as en, pt-BR or es-419, so YouTube does not treat it as another language. null clears a saved value. It does not turn off YouTube's automatic dubbing

aiGenerated.description: Disclose altered or synthetic content, such as an AI voice, an AI avatar or realistic footage that was generated or edited. YouTube shows its "Altered or synthetic content" label on the video. Omit it or send false for no label

youtubeConfigs.description: YouTube per-connection config with video title, tags, privacy, etc.

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this account, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, first comment, cover, collaborators, trial and audio, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators (Instagram Collab), up to 3. A leading @ is stripped and duplicates are dropped. Works on feed images, carousels and reels; a story or a trial reel with collaborators is refused with 400. Each collaborator gets an invite in Instagram and must accept it before the post shows on their profile

title.description: Track title, stored for display only

artist.description: Artist or creator, stored for display only

audioVolume.description: Volume of the added audio, 1 to 100. Defaults to 100

videoVolume.description: Volume of the video's own sound, 1 to 100. Defaults to 100

audio.description: Music or an original sound from Instagram's audio library, added to the Reel when it is published. Needs contentType VIDEO and a postType other than STORY, and only works for accounts with supportsInstagramAudio: true in list_accounts (connected through Facebook). Find ids with search_instagram_audio

trialGraduation.description: Publish a video reel as a trial reel: Instagram shows it to non-followers first and keeps it off followers' feeds and the profile grid until it is shared. MANUAL means the account owner shares it from the Instagram app; SS_PERFORMANCE means Instagram shares it if it performs well. Only for a single video posted as a reel or feed video, never a story, image or carousel (400 otherwise). Needs a professional account Instagram has enabled for trial reels; otherwise that platform fails with a message saying so

username.description: The public Instagram username to tag

x.description: Horizontal position of the tag on the image, from 0 (left edge) to 1 (right edge)

y.description: Vertical position of the tag on the image, from 0 (top edge) to 1 (bottom edge)

userTags.description: Public Instagram accounts tagged in the media, up to 20. Works on a single image, a single video (published as a Reel) or a single story; a carousel or several stories with tags is refused with 400. On a feed image every tag needs x and y; on a story they are optional, and on a video they are ignored because the person is tagged on the video as a whole. A leading @ is stripped and a repeated username keeps its first entry. If Instagram refuses a tag because the account is private or does not exist, the post goes out without its tags and instagramUntaggedUsernames in get_post lists the refused usernames

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Instagram shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on images, carousels, reels and stories, and a story made with shareToStory carries the label too. Omit it or send false for no label

instagramConfigs.description: Instagram per-connection config: post type (FEED, REEL, STORY), shareToStory, collaborators, user tags, the AI info label, Reel audio, and trial reels

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this page, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, video title and text background, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

textFormatPresetId.description: Facebook's id for a colored text background (for example 106018623298955 is solid purple, 249307305544279 is a red to blue gradient). Only for contentType TEXT posts with no media and text up to 130 characters; anything else is refused with 400. Links in the text show without a preview. If Facebook refuses the background, the post goes out as plain text

imageLayout.description: How a post with several images shows on Facebook. GRID is a photo grid. CAROUSEL is a swipeable carousel where each image is a card with its own link, and needs 2 to 5 images, no videos, postType FEED and one carouselCards entry per image; anything else is refused with 400

link.description: The http or https URL the card opens

title.description: The card's headline. Without it Facebook uses the linked page's title

description.description: The line under the headline, such as a price or the domain. Without it Facebook uses the linked page

carouselCards.description: One card per image, in the same order as the media, used when imageLayout is CAROUSEL. Facebook only shows your image, title and description on a card whose link points to a website the Page owns; for any other link the post fails with the error Facebook returns

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Facebook shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on every contentType VIDEO post, whatever its postType: Facebook publishes every video as a reel, and a video story carries the label too. Photos, carousels and text posts are rejected with a 400. Omit it or send false for no label

facebookConfigs.description: Facebook per-page config: post type, shareToStory, video title, text background, a grid or link carousel for several images, and the AI info label. pageId must match an entry in pageIds

boardId.description: Board id from list_pinterest_boards. Leave out boardId and boardName to pin to a public board named AdaptlyPost, created on the account the first time it is needed

boardName.description: The board's name, instead of boardId; never send both. Matched against this account's boards, exact first, then case-insensitive. A name no board has, or one several boards share, fails with 400 and never falls back to another board

title.description: Pin title (max 100 chars)

pinterestConfigs.description: Pinterest per-connection config: the board to pin to, a pin title and a destination link. Get boardId from list_pinterest_boards for that connectionId, or pass the board name as boardName instead (not both); a board belongs to one Pinterest account. A boardName that matches no board or several fails with 400. Without either the pin goes to a board named AdaptlyPost

connectionId.description: Google Business Profile account id from list_accounts

topicType.description: STANDARD is an update. EVENT and OFFER need eventTitle, eventStart and eventEnd

callToActionType.description: Button shown on the post. Every type except CALL needs callToActionUrl; CALL dials the phone number on the Business Profile

eventTitle.description: Title of the event or offer

eventStart.description: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm in the business's local time, with no offset (e.g. "2026-10-01T18:00"). Google reads event times in the location's time zone

eventEnd.description: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm in the business's local time, with no offset (e.g. "2026-10-01T21:00")

offerRedeemUrl.description: OFFER only: where the offer is redeemed

googleBusinessConfigs.description: Google Business Profile per-location config: update, event or offer, plus a button. connectionId must match an entry in googleBusinessConnectionIds. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters

connectionId.description: Tumblr blog account id from list_accounts

tags.description: Tumblr tags, without commas, up to 30. A leading # is stripped and duplicates are dropped, ignoring case

title.description: Shown as a heading above the media and the text

sourceUrl.description: Shown as the source link of the post

tumblrConfigs.description: Tumblr per-blog config: tags, a title and a source link. connectionId must match an entry in tumblrConnectionIds

connectionId.description: WordPress site account id from list_accounts

title.description: Post title. Defaults to the first line of the text, cut to 100 characters

excerpt.description: Summary WordPress shows in post lists and feeds

categoryIds.description: Category ids from list_wordpress_categories for this site. Omitted, WordPress files the post under the site's default category

tags.description: Tag names, up to 50. A tag the site does not have yet is created when the WordPress user may manage tags, and skipped otherwise

wordpressConfigs.description: WordPress per-site config: title, excerpt, categories and tags. connectionId must match an entry in wordpressConnectionIds

documentTitle.description: Title LinkedIn shows on a DOCUMENT post (max 100 chars). Defaults to the file name; ignored for other content types

reshareOf.description: Reshare this LinkedIn post from the account, with the post text as the commentary. Takes a urn:li:share: or urn:li:ugcPost: URN, such as the platformPostId from list_post_results, or a LinkedIn post link of the form https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/<urn>, which is also the link inside a post's Embed code. urn:li:activity: links are refused because LinkedIn cannot reshare them through its API. Media on the post is not attached on this account

linkedinConfigs.description: LinkedIn per-connection config: documentTitle names a DOCUMENT post, reshareOf reshares another LinkedIn post with the text as commentary. connectionId must match an entry in linkedinConnectionIds

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with postId, queuedPlatforms (platforms whose publishing job was queued; empty for scheduled posts and drafts), skippedPlatforms, isScheduled, and scheduledAt, plus recurringPostId when recurrence was sent. Publishing is asynchronous: check list_post_results for outcomes.

tools.name: validate_post
tools.title: Validate Post
tools.description: Dry-run create_post: takes exactly the same input and runs every check creating the post would run, plus the ones that usually fail only at publish time (TikTok creator limits, YouTube upload quota, expired tokens, Pinterest boards, X credits), without creating a post, uploading media or writing anything. Nothing is published, so no confirmation is needed. Always returns a report: valid is false when any issue has severity ERROR. Issues tied to one account are listed under that account in accounts (status READY, WARNING or BLOCKED); the rest are in issues, each with a stable code, severity and message. outcome says what creating the post would do (DRAFT, SCHEDULED or PUBLISH_NOW), and requiredPermissions names the permissions it would need; a missing one shows up as a PERMISSION_DENIED issue. notChecked lists what only the platform decides at publish time, so valid: true is not a guarantee. Fix every ERROR, then call create_post with the same input. Needs the posts.draft permission.

text.description: Default post text shared across platforms. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

accountIds.description: Account ids (or Facebook pageIds) from list_accounts to post to. AdaptlyPost adds each account's platform to platforms and its id to the matching connection-id array, so you can send these instead of platforms and the per-platform arrays, or alongside them. An id not connected to the workspace fails with 400

platforms.description: Target platforms (e.g. ["LINKEDIN", "TWITTER"]). Each one needs its matching connection-id array (pageIds for FACEBOOK, googleBusinessConnectionIds for GOOGLE_BUSINESS) filled with ids from list_accounts. Optional when accountIds is sent

contentType.description: Content type: TEXT, IMAGE, VIDEO, CAROUSEL, or DOCUMENT. Must match mediaUrls. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on TWITTER, BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text. DOCUMENT publishes one PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (max 100 MB, 300 pages) as a LinkedIn document post and is LinkedIn only: put exactly that one file in mediaUrls, target only LINKEDIN, and set the title with linkedinConfigs

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant to schedule (e.g. "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"). Omit to post immediately; a past time also posts immediately. With saveAsDraft it is the draft's planned date instead: nothing is scheduled, and publish_draft without a date later schedules the draft for it

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with the post for display (e.g. "America/New_York"); it does not shift scheduledAt

saveAsDraft.description: Save as DRAFT instead of publishing or scheduling; publish later with publish_draft. A scheduledAt sent with it is stored as the draft's planned date, and publish_draft schedules the draft for that date

frequency.description: How often the post repeats: DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or YEARLY. YEARLY repeats on the same date; a series started on February 29 posts on February 28 in other years

interval.description: Repeat every N days, weeks, months or years, 1 to 30 (default 1)

weekdays.description: WEEKLY only: the weekdays it goes out on (e.g. ["MONDAY", "THURSDAY"]). The weekday of scheduledAt is always included

endsOn.description: Last day an occurrence may go out on, as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Must be on or after the day of the first post. Cannot be combined with maxOccurrences

maxOccurrences.description: Total number of posts the series publishes, 2 to 365. Cannot be combined with endsOn; omit both to repeat until the user pauses or deletes the series

recurrence.description: Repeat the post on a schedule the user asked for, and confirm that schedule with them first. Needs a future scheduledAt, which becomes the first post and sets the time of day in timezone. Cannot be combined with saveAsDraft or TIKTOK. Missed slots, for example while paused, are skipped and never published late. The user can pause or stop the series at any time with pause_recurring_post or delete_recurring_post; list_recurring_posts shows it

mediaUrls.description: Media URLs to attach. Use publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls; the same publicUrl may be reused across posts. Do not reuse mediaUrls read back from a published post, which may be expiring platform links

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (max 1000 characters each; use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile and videos ignore it

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it
The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account right after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment is posted about 10 seconds after the platform publishes (60 on YouTube) and retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long reply, more than 25 replies, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

twitterKeepLinks.description: Keep links in the X text clickable. X charges over 10 times more for a post with a link, so by default every link in X text is broken (example.com becomes example. com). Only AppSumo lifetime deals can turn this on, and a kept link costs 20 credits instead of 2. true on any other plan is refused with 400; it is ignored when the X text has no link

tools.name: get_post
tools.title: Get Post
tools.description: Get one post's full record by id: text, contentType, status, scheduledAt, timezone, and a platforms array with each target's connection, status, errorMessage, and media. Visible only within the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another); any other id returns "Post not found or access denied". Use this to inspect content before update_post or publish_draft. Use list_post_results instead when you only need per-platform publishing outcomes and the platformIds for retry_failed_platforms, and list_posts to find ids by status, platform, or date. Post ids come from create_post, bulk_schedule_posts, or list_posts.

id.description: Post ID from create_post, bulk_schedule_posts, or list_posts

result.description: The full post record: id, status, contentType, text, scheduledAt, timezone, mediaUrls, createdAt, updatedAt, recurringPostId and occurrenceAt (set when the post is an occurrence of a recurring post; occurrenceAt is its slot in the series and stays the same when the post is rescheduled), and platforms (one entry per target with id, platform, connectionId or pageId, status, errorMessage, platformPostId, postUrl once published, mediaUrls, previewUrls, and the per-platform settings: firstComment with firstCommentStatus PENDING, PUBLISHED or FAILED, firstCommentError and firstCommentPublishedAt; threadReplies with threadStatus, threadReplyIds, threadError and threadPublishedAt; thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs overrides; mediaAspectRatio and mediaAspectRatioFit; instagramCollaborators, instagramUserTags, instagramUntaggedUsernames (tags Instagram refused), instagramAiGenerated, instagramUsername and instagramAudioId, instagramAudioTitle, instagramAudioArtist, instagramAudioVolume, instagramVideoVolume; facebookTextFormatPresetId, facebookImageLayout, facebookCarouselCards and facebookAiGenerated; youtubeAiGenerated and youtubeDefaultAudioLanguage; linkedinDocumentTitle and linkedinReshareOf; twitterKeepLinks; tumblrTags, tumblrTitle and tumblrSourceUrl; wordpressTitle, wordpressExcerpt, wordpressCategoryIds and wordpressTags; googleBusinessTopicType, googleBusinessCallToActionType, googleBusinessCallToActionUrl, googleBusinessEventTitle, googleBusinessEventStart, googleBusinessEventEnd and googleBusinessOffer fields). postUrl links to the published post on every platform; Instagram and Facebook stories expire after 24 hours, so for them it links to the profile or page. A shareToStory story is its own entry with postType STORY. previewUrls holds one permanent preview image per media item, a still frame for videos; after publishing, mediaUrls may become platform CDN links that expire within days, so show previewUrls instead.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.title: List Posts
tools.description: List posts in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another), any status, newest first by default. Returns { posts, total, hasMore }; each post carries its status and a platforms array with per-platform status. Filters: statuses, platforms (posts targeting any of them), and startDate/endDate, which bound scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled. limit is 1 to 100 (default 20); page with offset while hasMore is true. Use this to find post ids or check what is already queued. Use get_post for one post's full record and list_post_results for one post's per-platform outcomes and retry ids.

statuses.description: Filter by status (e.g. ["SCHEDULED", "DRAFT"]); omit for all statuses

platforms.description: Filter to posts targeting any of these platforms

startDate.description: Lower bound (ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-03-01") on scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled

endDate.description: Upper bound (ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-03-31") on scheduledAt, or createdAt for posts never scheduled

offset.description: Posts to skip; increase by limit while hasMore is true

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with posts (each with id, status, contentType, text, scheduledAt, timezone, recurringPostId and occurrenceAt for occurrences of a recurring post, and platforms with per-platform status), total (count of all matches), and hasMore.

tools.name: update_post
tools.title: Update Post
tools.description: Update a DRAFT or SCHEDULED post in place; any other status fails with "Cannot edit post in current state", so published posts cannot be changed. Updates are partial: text, contentType, scheduledAt, timezone, thumbnail fields, firstComments and platformThumbnails you omit keep their values; sending firstComments or platformThumbnails replaces every stored entry. The exception is platforms: sending it rebuilds the post's target set from this request alone, so include every connection-id array and platform config you want to keep (TikTok with privacyLevel, Pinterest with its boardId or boardName); omitting platforms leaves accounts, configs, and media untouched. mediaUrls only take effect together with platforms; use publicUrl values from upload_media. On SCHEDULED posts new media is verified in storage. Returns the updated post record. Use publish_draft to change a draft's status, unschedule_post to take a scheduled post off the calendar, delete_post to cancel, and create_post for a new post.

id.description: Post ID to update (must be DRAFT or SCHEDULED)

text.description: Updated text; omit to keep the current text. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platforms.description: New target platforms. Sending this replaces every target, so also resend the connection-id arrays and platform configs to keep; omit to leave targets unchanged

contentType.description: New content type; must match the media on the post. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on TWITTER, BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. DOCUMENT publishes one PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (max 100 MB, 300 pages) as a LinkedIn document post and is LinkedIn only: put exactly that one file in mediaUrls, target only LINKEDIN, and set the title with linkedinConfigs

scheduledAt.description: New schedule time as an absolute ISO 8601 instant; omit to keep. On a DRAFT it sets the planned date and the post stays a draft; null takes the planned date off a DRAFT and moves it off the calendar. On a SCHEDULED post null fails with 400 (use unschedule_post), and moving it more than a minute into the past fails with 400; use publish_draft to publish now

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored for display; does not shift scheduledAt

mediaUrls.description: Replacement media URLs, applied only when platforms is also sent. Use publicUrl values from upload_media or get_upload_urls

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (max 1000 characters each; use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile and videos ignore it. Applied only when platforms is also sent

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platformTexts.description: Per-platform caption overrides; applied to the targets sent in platforms

text.description: The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account right after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment is posted about 10 seconds after the platform publishes (60 on YouTube) and retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long reply, more than 25 replies, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

twitterKeepLinks.description: Keep links in the X text clickable. X charges over 10 times more for a post with a link, so by default every link in X text is broken (example.com becomes example. com). tools.name: delete_post
tools.title: Delete Post
tools.description: Delete a post record from AdaptlyPost by id. Use it to cancel a DRAFT or SCHEDULED post before it goes out; a deleted scheduled post will not publish. Deleting never removes content already on a network: for a COMPLETED or PARTIAL_FAILURE post this only drops AdaptlyPost's record, and the live posts stay up until removed on each platform. Prefer update_post to change a post instead of deleting and recreating it. A post in PUBLISHING fails with 409; wait for list_post_results to settle. Only posts in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) can be deleted; others return "Post not found or access denied". Returns { deleted: true }. Irreversible.

id.description: Post ID to delete, from list_posts or create_post

tools.name: unschedule_post
tools.title: Unschedule Post
tools.description: Take a DRAFT or SCHEDULED post off the calendar without deleting it: the post becomes an undated DRAFT (status DRAFT, scheduledAt null) and nothing publishes. Use it when the user wants to hold a scheduled post back; schedule it again later with publish_draft and a scheduledAt, and use delete_post only to drop it entirely. Any other status (PENDING, PUBLISHING, COMPLETED, FAILED, PARTIAL_FAILURE) fails with 400 because the post is already going out or out. Ids outside the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) return 404. Safe to repeat on a post that is already an undated draft. Returns the post record.

id.description: Post ID with status DRAFT or SCHEDULED, from list_posts or create_post

tools.name: publish_draft
tools.title: Publish Draft
tools.description: Publish a DRAFT post now or schedule it; SCHEDULED posts are accepted too, to reschedule or push live. Other statuses fail with "Post is not a draft". A future scheduledAt sets SCHEDULED for that time and queues nothing yet; a past one publishes now. Without scheduledAt, a draft whose planned date (the scheduledAt it was saved with) is still in the future is SCHEDULED for that date, and any other post (an undated draft, a planned date already past, a SCHEDULED post) publishes now. publishNow: true publishes now even when the draft has a planned date; sending it with scheduledAt fails with 400. Read the draft with get_post first and tell the user which of these will happen. Publishing now clears the stored scheduledAt, moves the post to PENDING and queues a publishing job per platform: content reaches the networks within moments and cannot be recalled. Fails if an account was disconnected or a TikTok entry lacks privacyLevel; fix with update_post first. Not for new content, use create_post. Check list_post_results afterwards for per-platform outcomes.

id.description: Post ID with status DRAFT (or SCHEDULED)

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant (e.g. "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"). A future time schedules for that time instead of the draft's planned date; a past time publishes now. Omit to schedule for the planned date when it is still in the future, and to publish now otherwise

publishNow.description: Publish now even when the draft has a planned date in the future. Sending it with scheduledAt fails with 400

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with the post for display (e.g. "America/New_York"); it does not shift scheduledAt

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

tools.name: list_post_results
tools.title: List Post Results
tools.description: Get one post's per-platform publishing outcomes: { postId, status, results[] } where each result has platformId, platform, accountName, status (PENDING, PUBLISHING, PUBLISHED, or FAILED), platformPostId, errorMessage, publishedAt, and tiktokDraftFallback (true when TikTok's daily cap sent the content to the TikTok inbox as a draft instead of publishing it; tell the user to finish it in the TikTok app). Each platform reports separately, so read every row instead of treating the post as one pass or fail. Call this after create_post, publish_draft, or retry_failed_platforms, since publishing is asynchronous and their responses only confirm queueing; poll until no row is PENDING or PUBLISHING. Take platformId from FAILED rows for retry_failed_platforms. Use get_post when you also need the content and schedule.

id.description: Post ID from create_post, publish_draft, bulk_schedule_posts, or list_posts

tools.name: retry_failed_platforms
tools.title: Retry Failed Platforms
tools.description: Re-queue publishing for a post's FAILED platforms. platformIds takes platformId values from list_post_results, platform names such as "BLUESKY" (every failed row of that platform), or can be omitted to retry every failed row. Only rows with status FAILED are reset to PENDING and retried with the same content. A value matching neither a row id nor a platform of the post fails with "Unknown retry target"; with nothing failed among the matches the call fails with "No failed platforms to retry". The post moves to PUBLISHING and the retry is asynchronous, so check list_post_results for the outcome. Read each errorMessage first and retry once the cause is fixed (reconnected account, replaced media), not for a platform-side restriction, which will just fail again. Content cannot change on retry.

id.description: Post ID whose platforms failed

platformIds.description: platformId values from list_post_results or platform names such as "BLUESKY". Omit to retry every FAILED row

tools.name: bulk_schedule_posts
tools.title: Bulk Schedule Posts
tools.description: Schedule up to 100 posts in one call to the same platforms and accounts. Each item supplies its own text, contentType, scheduledAt, and optional media; platforms, connection-id arrays, timezone, and platform configs are shared by every item, though an item may carry its own tiktokConfigs, youtubeConfigs, instagramConfigs, facebookConfigs, pinterestConfigs, googleBusinessConfigs, tumblrConfigs or wordpressConfigs to replace the shared ones, plus its own firstComments, threadReplies, platformThumbnails and platformAspectRatios. twitterKeepLinks and linkedinConfigs are not available in bulk. Call validate_bulk_posts with the same input first to see the problems of every item without creating anything. Items are processed independently: each is validated and created like create_post, so one bad item fails alone while the rest are scheduled. Returns { totalScheduled, totalFailed, results[] } with a postId or errorMessage per item, in input order; read every row. An item with a past scheduledAt publishes immediately rather than being rejected. Call list_accounts first; TikTok needs tiktokConfigs with privacyLevel, and Pinterest takes pinterestConfigs with a boardId from list_pinterest_boards or a boardName, not both; an item whose boardName matches no board or several fails alone. Use create_post for a single post or a draft; this tool has no draft mode. These posts publish publicly to the user's social accounts: show the user every item's text, media and time plus the accounts, and get their confirmation before calling. Each call creates new posts, so calling again after an error or timeout can publish duplicates; check list_posts first.

platforms.description: Target platforms shared by every item. Each needs its connection-id array (pageIds for FACEBOOK, googleBusinessConnectionIds for GOOGLE_BUSINESS)

timezone.description: IANA timezone stored with every post for display; does not shift scheduledAt

text.description: Post text/caption. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

contentType.description: TEXT, IMAGE, VIDEO, or CAROUSEL; must match mediaUrls. DOCUMENT posts cannot be bulk scheduled; use create_post. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on TWITTER, BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text
