thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platformTexts.description: Per-platform caption overrides for this item

text.description: The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account right after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment is posted about 10 seconds after the platform publishes (60 on YouTube) and retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long reply, more than 25 replies, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, first comment, cover, collaborators, trial and audio, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

MANUAL means the account owner shares it from the Instagram app; SS_PERFORMANCE means Instagram shares it if it performs well. Only for a single video posted as a reel or feed video, never a story, image or carousel (400 otherwise). Needs a professional account Instagram has enabled for trial reels; otherwise that platform fails with a message saying so

A leading @ is stripped and a repeated username keeps its first entry. Nothing is published, so no confirmation is needed. Each report has valid, outcome, requiredPermissions, issues, accounts and notChecked, as in validate_post. Fix the items with ERROR issues, then call bulk_schedule_posts. Needs the posts.draft permission.

text.description: Post text/caption. On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

contentType.description: TEXT, IMAGE, VIDEO, or CAROUSEL; must match mediaUrls. DOCUMENT posts cannot be bulk scheduled; use create_post. CAROUSEL takes 2 or more items in mediaUrls, up to 4 on TWITTER, BLUESKY and MASTODON, 5 on PINTEREST, 10 on INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, THREADS and TELEGRAM, 20 on LINKEDIN and WORDPRESS, 30 on TUMBLR and 35 on TIKTOK (JPEG or WebP photos only). INSTAGRAM and THREADS accept images and videos in the same carousel; every other platform takes images only, and YOUTUBE has no carousel. GOOGLE_BUSINESS takes TEXT or IMAGE with one JPEG or PNG image up to 5 MB, and text up to 1500 characters. TELEGRAM takes text up to 4096 characters, up to 10 images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (50 MB); a caption over 1024 characters goes out as its own message after the media. WORDPRESS publishes the text as the body of a blog post, up to 100,000 characters: blank lines start new paragraphs and bare links become clickable. It takes up to 20 JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF images (20 MB each) or one MP4 or MOV video (500 MB); the first image is the featured image and the other images or the video follow the text

scheduledAt.description: Absolute ISO 8601 instant; a past time publishes immediately

mediaUrls.description: publicUrl values from upload_media; unstored URLs fail this item

mediaAltTexts.description: Alt text per image, in the same order as mediaUrls (max 1000 characters each; use "" to skip an image). Sent to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, WordPress, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and Threads; Pinterest uses the first one (cut to 500). TikTok, YouTube, Google Business Profile and videos ignore it

thumbnailUrl.description: Video thumbnail as an https URL or an image data URI, used on every platform that takes one unless platformThumbnails overrides it

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: Video frame timestamp (ms) to use as the thumbnail on every platform that takes one: YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST, TELEGRAM and TIKTOK. A thumbnailUrl sent with it wins everywhere except TIKTOK, which takes only a frame, and platformThumbnails overrides both

text.description: On LinkedIn, mention a company page with @[Page Name](urn:li:organization:<id>), using the page name exactly as LinkedIn shows it

platformTexts.description: Per-platform caption overrides for this item

text.description: The comment's text, trimmed. The limit depends on the platform, see firstComments

firstComments.description: A comment posted from the same account right after the post goes out on a platform, one entry per platform. Available on LINKEDIN (1250 characters), TWITTER (280, as a reply), BLUESKY (300, as a reply), MASTODON (500, as a reply), YOUTUBE (10000), FACEBOOK (8000) and INSTAGRAM (2200). A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long comment, a second entry for one platform, a platform that also has threadReplies, a private or made for kids YouTube video and Facebook or Instagram stories are refused with 400. The comment is posted about 10 seconds after the platform publishes (60 on YouTube) and retried up to 3 times; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for it like any X post. A Facebook Page or Instagram account connected before first comments came to them must be reconnected once; until then its comment fails and firstCommentError says to reconnect. A comment that fails never fails the post: read firstCommentStatus and firstCommentError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every first comment and omitting it keeps the stored ones

texts.description: The replies in order, each trimmed. The limit per reply depends on the platform, see threadReplies

threadReplies.description: Turns the post into a thread: the post opens it and each text is published as a reply to the one before, from the same account, one entry per platform. Available on TWITTER (280 characters per reply, or the account's own limit on X Premium), BLUESKY (300) and MASTODON (500, or the instance's limit), up to 25 replies. A platform the post does not go to, an empty or too long reply, more than 25 replies, a second entry for one platform and a platform that also has a first comment are refused with 400. An entry with an empty texts array removes the thread. Replies start about 10 seconds after the platform publishes, 2 seconds apart. A failed run is retried up to 3 times and resumes after the last reply that went out; on X it is not retried, and a lifetime-deal account pays for each reply like any X post. A thread that fails never fails the post: read threadStatus, threadReplyIds and threadError on the platform in get_post. On an update, sending the array replaces every thread and omitting it keeps the stored ones

thumbnailUrl.description: The image to use as this platform's thumbnail, an https URL or an image data URI

thumbnailTimestampMs.description: The video frame (ms from the start) to use as this platform's thumbnail

platformThumbnails.description: A different thumbnail for one platform of a VIDEO post, one entry per platform. A platform without an entry uses the post-level thumbnailUrl and thumbnailTimestampMs. YOUTUBE, FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, PINTEREST and TELEGRAM take an image (thumbnailUrl) or a frame (thumbnailTimestampMs), the image winning when both are sent; TIKTOK takes only a frame. Posts that are not videos, Facebook and Instagram stories, a second entry for one platform and an entry the platform cannot use are refused with 400. On an update, sending the array replaces every override and omitting it keeps the stored ones

aspectRatio.description: SQUARE is 1:1, PORTRAIT 4:5, VERTICAL 9:16 and LANDSCAPE 1.91:1

fit.description: How an image of another shape reaches the ratio. CROP (the default) cuts it from the center; PAD keeps the whole image and fills the rest with a blurred copy of it

platformAspectRatios.description: Reframe every image of an IMAGE or CAROUSEL post to one shape on a platform, one entry per platform. INSTAGRAM takes SQUARE, PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE (Instagram refuses 9:16 feed and carousel images); TIKTOK takes all four. Video posts, Instagram stories and a second entry for the same platform are refused with 400. Omit a platform to keep its images as uploaded. On an update it applies to the mediaUrls sent in the same request

postType.description: Where the post goes: FEED works with every content type, REEL needs contentType VIDEO, STORY needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL (a CAROUSEL story publishes each media item as its own story, in order). Any other combination is refused with 400

shareToStory.description: Also publish the same media as a story on this account, next to the FEED or REEL post. The story shows as its own entry in platforms with postType STORY, so it succeeds, fails and retries on its own. It skips the caption, first comment, cover, collaborators, trial and audio, needs IMAGE, VIDEO or CAROUSEL, and a video must fit the story length limit (60 seconds). Ignored when postType is STORY

collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators (Instagram Collab), up to 3. A leading @ is stripped and duplicates are dropped. Works on feed images, carousels and reels; a story or a trial reel with collaborators is refused with 400. Each collaborator gets an invite in Instagram and must accept it before the post shows on their profile

title.description: Track title, stored for display only

artist.description: Artist or creator, stored for display only

audioVolume.description: Volume of the added audio, 1 to 100. Defaults to 100

videoVolume.description: Volume of the video's own sound, 1 to 100. Defaults to 100

audio.description: Music or an original sound from Instagram's audio library, added to the Reel when it is published. Needs contentType VIDEO and a postType other than STORY, and only works for accounts with supportsInstagramAudio: true in list_accounts (connected through Facebook). Find ids with search_instagram_audio

trialGraduation.description: Publish a video reel as a trial reel: Instagram shows it to non-followers first and keeps it off followers' feeds and the profile grid until it is shared. MANUAL means the account owner shares it from the Instagram app; SS_PERFORMANCE means Instagram shares it if it performs well. Only for a single video posted as a reel or feed video, never a story, image or carousel (400 otherwise). Needs a professional account Instagram has enabled for trial reels; otherwise that platform fails with a message saying so

username.description: The public Instagram username to tag

y.description: Vertical position of the tag on the image, from 0 (top edge) to 1 (bottom edge)

userTags.description: Public Instagram accounts tagged in the media, up to 20. Works on a single image, a single video (published as a Reel) or a single story; a carousel or several stories with tags is refused with 400. On a feed image every tag needs x and y; on a story they are optional, and on a video they are ignored because the person is tagged on the video as a whole. A leading @ is stripped and a repeated username keeps its first entry. If Instagram refuses a tag because the account is private or does not exist, the post goes out without its tags and instagramUntaggedUsernames in get_post lists the refused usernames

aiGenerated.description: Disclose that the post was made or edited with AI. Instagram shows its "AI info" label on the post. Works on images, carousels, reels and stories, and a story made with shareToStory carries the label too. Omit it or send false for no label

instagramConfigs.description: Instagram config for this item only; replaces the batch-level instagramConfigs

Only for contentType TEXT posts with no media and text up to 130 characters; anything else is refused with 400. Links in the text show without a preview. If Facebook refuses the background, the post goes out as plain text

imageLayout.description: How a post with several images shows on Facebook. GRID is a photo grid. CAROUSEL is a swipeable carousel where each image is a card with its own link, and needs 2 to 5 images, no videos, postType FEED and one carouselCards entry per image; anything else is refused with 400

description.description: The line under the headline, such as a price or the domain. Without it Facebook uses the linked page

carouselCards.description: One card per image, in the same order as the media, used when imageLayout is CAROUSEL. Facebook only shows your image, title and description on a card whose link points to a website the Page owns; for any other link the post fails with the error Facebook returns

Works on every contentType VIDEO post, whatever its postType: Facebook publishes every video as a reel, and a video story carries the label too. Photos, carousels and text posts are rejected with a 400. Omit it or send false for no label

tools.name: list_recurring_posts
tools.title: List Recurring Posts
tools.description: List the recurring posts (series) in the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another), created by passing recurrence to create_post. Returns { recurringPosts, total, hasMore }; each series has id, status (ACTIVE, PAUSED or ENDED), pauseReason when paused, frequency, interval, weekdays, startsAt, timezone, endsOn or maxOccurrences, nextOccurrenceAt, occurrenceCount, and the content and platforms every occurrence copies. Only the next occurrence of an ACTIVE series exists as a SCHEDULED post, created about 24 hours ahead; list_posts shows it with recurringPostId set. A series pauses itself after 3 failed posts in a row, when the subscription lapses, when its creator loses workspace access, when one of its accounts is disconnected, or when a platform rejects the content; pauseReason and lastError say which. limit is 1 to 100 (default 20); page with offset while hasMore is true. Editing a series or skipping one date is only possible in the AdaptlyPost app.

statuses.description: Filter by status (e.g. ["ACTIVE", "PAUSED"]); omit for all statuses

offset.description: Recurring posts to skip; increase by limit while hasMore is true

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with recurringPosts (each with id, status, pauseReason, lastError, frequency, interval, weekdays, startsAt, timezone, endsOn, maxOccurrences, nextOccurrenceAt, occurrenceCount, contentType, text, mediaUrls, platformTypes, and platforms), total (count of all matches), and hasMore.

tools.name: get_recurring_post
tools.title: Get Recurring Post
tools.description: Get one recurring post (series) by id: status, pauseReason and lastError when paused, the schedule (frequency, interval, weekdays, startsAt, timezone, endsOn, maxOccurrences), nextOccurrenceAt (the next slot not yet created as a post; absent once ENDED), occurrenceCount (posts created so far), and the content and platforms each occurrence copies. Ids outside the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) return "Recurring post not found". Ids come from list_recurring_posts, the recurringPostId returned by create_post, or the recurringPostId on a post from get_post or list_posts.

id.description: Recurring post ID from list_recurring_posts, create_post, or a post's recurringPostId

tools.name: pause_recurring_post
tools.title: Pause Recurring Post
tools.description: Pause a recurring post: it stops creating occurrences and deletes its upcoming SCHEDULED post, preventing future scheduled occurrences until resume_recurring_post; an occurrence already publishing may still complete. Posts already published are kept. Slots that pass while paused are skipped, never published later. Use it when the user wants to hold the series; use delete_recurring_post to stop it for good. Deleting only the upcoming post with delete_post skips that one date and the series continues. Ids outside the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) return "Recurring post not found". Returns the recurring post with status PAUSED and pauseReason USER.

id.description: Recurring post ID to pause, from list_recurring_posts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: The paused recurring post: id, status PAUSED, pauseReason USER, the schedule, occurrenceCount, and the content and platforms.

tools.name: resume_recurring_post
tools.title: Resume Recurring Post
tools.description: Resume a PAUSED recurring post. It continues from the next occurrence after now; slots missed while paused are not published. The next occurrence is created as a SCHEDULED post about 24 hours before it goes out and then publishes to the networks, so confirm with the user first. If the series has no slot left (endsOn passed or maxOccurrences reached) it comes back ENDED instead. When pauseReason is CONNECTION_REMOVED, ACCESS_LOST, SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE or INVALID_CONTENT, fix the cause first or the series pauses again. Ids outside the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) return "Recurring post not found". Returns the recurring post with its new status and nextOccurrenceAt.

id.description: Recurring post ID to resume, from list_recurring_posts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: The resumed recurring post: id, status (ACTIVE, or ENDED when no slot is left), nextOccurrenceAt, the schedule, occurrenceCount, and the content and platforms.

tools.name: delete_recurring_post
tools.title: Delete Recurring Post
tools.description: Delete a recurring post: the series stops for good and its upcoming SCHEDULED post is deleted. Posts that already went out are kept. Prefer pause_recurring_post when the user may want the series back. To skip a single date, delete that occurrence with delete_post instead; the series continues. Ids outside the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another) return "Recurring post not found". Returns { deleted: true }. Irreversible.

id.description: Recurring post ID to delete, from list_recurring_posts

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to act in the workspace list_workspaces marks current. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace (accounts, posts, uploads) do not exist in another

result.description: An object with deleted: true once the recurring post is removed.

tools.name: list_rss_feeds
tools.title: List RSS Feeds
tools.description: List the RSS and Atom feeds connected to the workspace (the current one unless workspaceId names another), newest first; a workspace holds at most 20. Each new item of a feed becomes a post on its targets. A feed pauses itself after 5 failed fetches in a row (FETCH_FAILURES), 3 items in a row that failed to post (CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES), when its owner loses the permission its post mode needs (ACCESS_LOST), when the plan no longer covers publishing (SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE) or when every target account was disconnected (CONNECTION_REMOVED); pauseReason and lastError say which. Needs the posts.read permission. Takes only the optional workspaceId.

tools.name: create_rss_feed

tools.description: Connect an RSS or Atom feed so each new item becomes a post on the target accounts. The feed is fetched and every item already in it is recorded, so only items that appear later are posted; postLatestItem also posts the newest one on the first check. The feed is then checked every checkIntervalMinutes and posts as the member who saved it, as a draft, a scheduled post or straight away (postMode). With postMode SCHEDULE or PUBLISH, posts go out on the user's accounts without further confirmation, so confirm the feed, the accounts, the mode and the text with the user first. Try preview_rss_feed first to show what the posts will say. Fails with 400 for invalid settings, a URL that is not a feed, a feed already connected or the 20-feed workspace limit, and 503 when the feed cannot be reached. Needs posts.draft, plus the permission of the post mode.
